 Pre-Admission Settlement Under IBC: Can a Corporate Insolvency Proceeding Be Withdrawn After Admission?
 Priyanshi Garg 
 Priyanshi Garg 
 Author 
 Follow 
 View profile 
 Last updated: 21 November 2026 
 Save 
 Share 
 Join Us 
 Follow Us 
 Add as Source 
 The honest answer after the 2026 amendment is: only through a narrow door. Settlement is easiest before admission and hardest after the first call for resolution plans.
 What Section 12A now says
 The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (Amendment) Act, 2026 substituted section 12A, in force from 26 May 2026. An admitted application under section 7, 9 or 10 can be withdrawn only if:
 the resolution professional applies (no longer the applicant creditor)
 the committee of creditors (CoC) has been constituted 
 the first invitation for resolution plans has not yet been issued
 90% of the CoC’s voting share approves
 the NCLT decides within 30 days 
 The Windows
 Stage 
 Position 
 Before admission 
 The applicant can withdraw with the NCLT’s leave, and settlement is the cleanest route 
 After admission, before the CoC exists 
 Not under section 12A. The 2026 amendment closed this window. Even where parties settle, the NCLAT has indicated that the IRP must move the NCLT under section 12A when the statutory window opens 
 After the CoC, before the first invitation for plans 
 Section 12A: RP application, 90% CoC approval, NCLT order 
 After the first invitation for plans 
 Barred under section 12A 
 Why the change
 Under the old regime, withdrawal could be sought before the CoC was constituted, and commentary notes that settlement exits accounted for roughly 14% of admitted CIRPs, many initiated by operational creditors. The Supreme Court’s reported decision in the Byju’s matter rejected a withdrawal that bypassed the section 12A route through the NCLAT’s inherent powers. In Vallal RCK , it had earlier upheld the 90% requirement and said adjudicating authorities should not ordinarily sit in appeal over a CoC’s decision.
 The same amendment makes admission more mechanical. Once default is shown, the NCLT must admit a section 7 application, and it must decide admission within 14 days, with reasons if it takes longer.
 What it means for settlement planning
 Settle before admission. After that, the settlement clock runs against the CoC timetable.
 Don’t wait. If you must settle after admission, make sure the CoC is constituted quickly and that the RP is willing to file.
 Count the votes. Ninety percent of the CoC means all large financial creditors must agree.
 Mind the structural gap. An operational creditor that settled may no longer control withdrawal, because it doesn’t vote on the CoC.
 Last resort. After Form G, the Supreme Court’s Article 142 power has been used in the past, but sparingly.
 Bottom line: Under the 2026 regime, the best “pre-admission settlement” is the one done before admission. Afterwards, the exit is a collective decision.
